# Design prototype and validate a physical product

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before committing a physical product design to tooling, production or customer release. A versioned design and prototype evidence pack with reviewed acceptance criteria and an explicit production decision.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> Operational draft. Source checked on 2026-10-30. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance, certification or completed execution is claimed. The source context is design methodology. Resolve applicable law and expert review before external action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Frame the user need and operating constraints

agent-runnable


Collect evidence of the user problem, intended environment, target cost and product claims. Identify uncertain assumptions and the people who can validate them.

- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Define engineering safety and regulatory criteria

human · human approval required · hard to undo


Qualified engineering and specialist owners select relevant performance, safety and market-access criteria. Record required testing and stop conditions before exposing people to prototype risks.

- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare design alternatives and a test plan

agent-runnable


Document candidate designs, materials and expected failure modes. Specify measurable experiments and evidence needed to select a design without presenting a concept model as verified hardware.

- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Build and test controlled prototypes

human · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized competent personnel build and test prototypes using suitable facilities and protective controls. Record configuration, measurements and failures; stop unsafe trials and investigate before continuing.

- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review evidence and resolve design risks

human · human approval required · hard to undo


Engineering owners compare results with acceptance criteria and customer observations. Assign remediation and repeat testing when changes affect the safety or performance evidence.

- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Approve the design transfer decision

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The accountable owner approves revision-controlled drawings, requirements and remaining conditions for manufacturing. Keep required certification and production qualification as separate gates rather than claiming prototype success authorizes sale.

- Verify: A versioned design and prototype evidence pack with reviewed acceptance criteria and an explicit production decision.
- Sources: [Design Council Framework for Innovation](https://www.designcouncil.org.uk/resources/framework-for-innovation/)
